definitions.gloss: before something happens, in advance, preventive
definitions.explanation: The state before something (usually something undesirable) has occurred. Almost always used in the phrase 未然に防ぐ (to prevent before it happens). In grammar, refers to the irrealis or imperfective form of a verb.

examples.japanese: {事故|じこ}を{未然|みぜん}に{防|ふせ}ぐ。
examples.english: To prevent an accident before it happens.

examples.japanese: {犯罪|はんざい}を{未然|みぜん}に{防止|ぼうし}することが{重要|じゅうよう}だ。
examples.english: It is important to prevent crime before it occurs.

examples.japanese: {定期|ていき}{検査|けんさ}を{行|おこな}うことで、{設備|せつび}の{故障|こしょう}を{未然|みぜん}に{防|ふせ}ぐことができる。
examples.english: By conducting regular inspections, equipment malfunctions can be prevented before they happen.

notes:
USAGE:
{未然|みぜん} is almost always used in the fixed phrase {未然|みぜん}に{防|ふせ}ぐ (to prevent before it happens) or {未然|みぜん}に{防止|ぼうし}する. It is rarely used independently outside this pattern.

In Japanese grammar, {未然形|みぜんけい} (irrealis form) is the name of the first verb conjugation base, used before endings like ない (negative) and れる/られる (passive). The term literally means "the form of what has not yet happened."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {未然|みぜん}に{防|ふせ}ぐ: to prevent before it happens
- {未然|みぜん}に{防止|ぼうし}する: to prevent in advance
- {未然|みぜん}{形|けい}: irrealis form (grammar term)
